subject: ventures/freelance-contract-checker
auditor: agent session (Claude), quality round 119, see run record
professional: a contracts attorney who reviews freelance and independent-contractor agreements for creative and software freelancers (or a senior freelancer-contracts reviewer of the Freelancers Union / AIGA kind); they check first that the payment term is read correctly whatever the phrasing (net N, within N days of invoice/completion/acceptance), that IP passes only on payment and is limited to the deliverables, that kill fee / termination pay, revision caps and change orders are spotted, that indemnity and liability caps are read clause by clause rather than anywhere in the document, and that the output never reads as a legal opinion

evidence.correctness: Probe scripts /tmp/claude-0/fcc/probe.mjs and /tmp/claude-0/fcc/days.mjs run against the shipped calc.mjs. Pass against outside sources: NYC Freelance Isn't Free Act (NYC Admin Code 20-929; NY State FIFA 2024 same rule) treats 30 days as the default payment window, and 'Invoices are payable net 30.' gives days 30 and no slow-payment finding; net 45 and 'within forty-five (45) days of receipt of invoice' give 45 and slow-payment medium; 'Contractor must work set hours ... on-site' gives employee-control (IRS behavioural-control factors). Fail: paymentDays (calc.mjs:26) has an optional lazy word group '(\w[\w -]*?)' before the digits, so it swallows leading digits: 'Client shall pay within 90 days of receipt of invoice.' -> 0, 'within 90 days of completion' -> 0, 'within 120 days of acceptance' -> 20; a full contract paying 'within 90 days of completion' (three times the FIFA default) returns verdict no-red-flags. 'Payment due 75 days after invoice date' and 'paid 90 days after receipt' (the second is named in the code comment at calc.mjs:21 as handled) -> null. False negatives on high-severity clauses: 'Contractor shall be liable for all damages, including consequential damages and lost profits' -> no liability finding (any 'liab' suppresses it, calc.mjs:146); indemnity 'from all claims of any kind' plus an unrelated 'Expenses shall not exceed $200' -> no uncapped-indemnity (calc.mjs:141); 'Client may terminate ... upon 10 days written notice, and no further fees shall be owed' -> no terminate-no-pay (only 'at any time/for convenience/without cause' trigger it); 'shall not engage in any business that competes with Client' for two years -> no non-compete; 'Contractor will begin work upon payment of the deposit. Contractor hereby assigns ... upon creation' -> no ip-before-payment; 'Contractor will make all revisions Client requests' -> no revision finding. False positives: 'This Agreement contains no non-compete' -> non-compete HIGH; 'A late fee applies to invoices that remain unpaid after 60 days' with net 15 -> slow-payment HIGH at 60 days. Of 16 probe contracts, 10 gave a wrong or missing finding on a clause the page says it checks. The core payment reader is wrong on common phrasing, so 1.
evidence.completeness: Every rule the README, VENTURE.yaml and page list exists in calc.mjs and runs end to end through index.html: slow payment, pay-when-paid, deposit, late fee, IP before payment, IP too broad, portfolio right, unlimited/unstated revisions, change order, acceptance, termination no pay, one-sided termination, non-compete, non-solicit, uncapped indemnity, liability cap, absolute warranty, perpetual NDA, employee control, venue, fee shifting; text-file input, paste, worked example, text checklist and CSV downloads (formula-injection guard), print, local usage counter with opt-out. No stubs or TODOs; related-tool links checked by page.test.mjs (freelance-contract-maker exists). Served copy clean (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs freelance-contract-checker: no placeholder or retired origin). The features exist; that they misfire is scored under correctness, so 3.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/freelance-contract-checker && node --test '*.test.mjs': 20 pass, 0 fail; the README's root-relative command also passes 20. Five mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: severity threshold 'days >= 60' -> 'days > 60' (calc.mjs:58) SURVIVED; liability-cap rule disabled with 'if (false)' (calc.mjs:146) SURVIVED; payment anchors reduced to invoice|receipt only (calc.mjs:26) SURVIVED; Math.max -> Math.min (calc.mjs:29) caught; indemnity cap regex made to match every indemnity (calc.mjs:141) caught. 3 of 5 survive. Tests check one bad sample and one good contract; no test has a payment term tied to completion or acceptance, no negated clause, no clause-scoped cap, so the existing digit-swallowing bug in paymentDays is invisible to the suite. 2.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (213 lines), index.html (183), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs. Pure, dependency-free module, escaped HTML output, CSV formula guard, guarded localStorage. Defects: every rule is a regex over the whole normalised document, so conditions that belong to one clause are met anywhere (cap 'not exceed' in an expense clause caps the indemnity, 'upon payment of the deposit' makes an assignment conditional, any 'liab' counts as a liability cap); no sentence or clause segmentation; no negation handling; the optional lazy capture in paymentDays (calc.mjs:26) is a classic regex bug; days 0 is shown as 'not found' because of truthiness (calc.mjs:190, index.html:153). A senior JS reviewer would ask for clause segmentation and a table of phrased fixtures before accepting, so 2.
evidence.claims: Backed: 'nothing uploaded' (page.test.mjs asserts no fetch/XHR/beacon/WebSocket and local-only imports); disclaimer 'not legal, tax, accounting, compliance, or financial advice', 'A clean result means these rules found nothing, not that a contract is safe' (index.html:120); 'Not decided' list (index.html:95); output text says 'not legal advice ... Have an attorney review' (calc.mjs:196). No unauthorised-practice-of-law framing: it never says a clause is enforceable or the contract is safe. FAQ copyright answer ('Without a written assignment you usually keep copyright') agrees with 17 U.S.C. 201(a)-(b). Usage events listed in the footer match index.html calls. Unbacked or weaker than stated: meta description and llms.txt promise to flag 'no kill fee' (index.html:7, llms.txt:3) but termination on notice with no pay is missed; the comment at calc.mjs:21 says 'paid 90 days after receipt' is parsed and it returns null; llms.txt:5 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in' is calculator boilerplate on a text checker. Stage 'prototype' and the 'Unverified' note in VENTURE.yaml are honest. 2.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job as a freelance designer pasting a client agreement before signing: paste, optional fee and wait, Check. On the shipped sample (net 60, pay-when-paid, WFH assignment, unlimited revisions, terminate without cause, non-compete, uncapped indemnity, error-free warranty) every trap is flagged with a concrete ask, and the downloadable checklist is usable as a negotiation list. On realistic rewordings of the same traps (payment within 90 days of completion, liable for consequential damages, terminate on notice with no fees owed, 'competes with Client') it says 'No red flags found by these rules' or misses the worst clause, and it flags a contract that explicitly says it has no non-compete. The 'found by these rules' wording and footer hedge it, but a freelancer without a lawyer is the user, and they would act on a clean result. 2.
evidence.domain: Compared against Freelancers Union model contract terms and the AIGA standard agreement (deposit, kill fee, defined revision rounds, change orders, IP on full payment, pre-existing materials retained, portfolio right, liability capped at fees, fee-shifting), NYC/NY State Freelance Isn't Free Act (30-day default, written contract), and 17 U.S.C. 101 work-made-for-hire. The checklist and the 'ask for' wording match practice. Departures: no note that a contractor's website or software is generally not one of the nine 101(2) work-for-hire categories (so the clause works only as an assignment) or that in California a work-for-hire clause with an individual makes them an employee for some statutes (Labor Code 3351.5(c), Unemployment Ins. Code 686); governing law/venue flagged only when arbitration also appears (calc.mjs:164), so 'exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Delaware' passes silently; no mention of FIFA's statutory 30-day rule and anti-retaliation rights where they apply; no auto-renewal, payment-in-equity or expense-reimbursement checks. The method (whole-document regex) is below what a reviewer would sign off for clause detection. 2.

defects.what: paymentDays' optional lazy word group swallows leading digits: 'within 90 days of receipt of invoice' -> 0, 'within 90 days of completion' -> 0, 'within 120 days of acceptance' -> 20, so a 90-day-from-completion contract gets no slow-payment finding and verdict no-red-flags

the liability rule is suppressed by any 'liab' or 'consequential' in the document, so 'Contractor shall be liable for all damages, including consequential damages and lost profits' produces no liability finding
an indemnity counts as capped if 'limited to', 'not exceed' or 'capped' appears anywhere (e.g. an expense limit), so an all-claims indemnity is not flagged
'upon ... payment' anywhere (e.g. 'begin work upon payment of the deposit') makes an assignment 'upon creation' read as payment-conditional, so ip-before-payment is missed

termination on notice with no fees owed is not flagged as termination without pay / no kill fee; only 'at any time', 'for convenience' or 'without cause' trigger it, though the page promises to flag 'no kill fee'
no negation or rephrasing handling for restrictive covenants: 'shall not engage in any business that competes with Client' is missed, 'This Agreement contains no non-compete' is flagged HIGH
a late-fee sentence ('invoices that remain unpaid after 60 days') is read as the payment term, giving slow-payment HIGH on a net 15 contract
open-ended revisions phrased without a keyword ('Contractor will make all revisions Client requests') give no revision finding at all, because any 'revision' word suppresses no-revision-limit

3 of 5 seeded mutants survive (severity threshold, liability rule removed, completion/acceptance anchors removed); tests use one bad and one good contract and no phrasing variants or negations, which is why the paymentDays bug shipped

work-for-hire flagged without the 17 U.S.C. 101 point that a contractor's website or software is usually not a work-for-hire category (the clause works only as an assignment) or the California Labor Code 3351.5(c) employee-status effect
governing law and venue are flagged only when arbitration also appears, so an exclusive out-of-state court venue passes silently
comment says 'paid 90 days after receipt' is parsed; it returns null, as does 'Payment due 75 days after invoice date'
a parsed 0 days is shown as 'not found' / 'none' because of a truthiness test, hiding the parser bug from the user
'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in' is calculator boilerplate on a text checker

verdict: Does not meet the bar (correctness 1, claims 2, verification 2, median 2); finished (completeness 3). Every rule the page lists exists and the framing is safe: not legal advice, no-upload enforced by a test, a clean result explicitly not a safety opinion, and the 'ask for' wording matches Freelancers Union and AIGA practice. On the shipped sample every trap is caught. On realistic rewordings it is unreliable: the payment-day parser swallows digits ('within 90 days of receipt of invoice' -> 0, 'within 120 days of acceptance' -> 20), so a contract paying 90 days after completion, three times the Freelance Isn't Free Act default, gets 'No red flags found by these rules'; liability, indemnity and IP-on-payment rules are satisfied by words anywhere in the document; termination on notice with no pay, a 'competes with' covenant and 'all revisions Client requests' are missed, while 'contains no non-compete' is flagged high. 10 of 16 probe contracts gave a wrong or missing finding, and 3 of 5 seeded mutants survive. It is a free MIT lead magnet; freelancer products are 'Not now' in bets.md and no paid product sits behind it.
